articleTitle: Keynote Speech III: Evaluating a System's Effectiveness with Approximate Data
publicationTitle: 2018 28th International Conference on Computer Theory and Applications (ICCTA)
abstract: Summary form only given, as follows. The complete presentation was not made available for publication as part of the conference proceedings. The Grey System theory introduced by Deng in 1982 has been nowadays proved to be an effective tool for studying systems with “poor” (uncertain, incomplete, etc.) In the present research Grey Numbers are used as tools for evaluating a system's mean performance when utilizing qualitative grades and not numerical scores for this purpose. Although this new assessment method is proved to be equivalent with an analogous method using Triangular Fuzzy Numbers as tools developed in an earlier work, it reduces the required computational burden, since it requires the calculation of two components only (instead of three in the case of the Triangular Fuzzy Numbers) for obtaining the mean value of the Grey Numbers involved. Examples are also presented on student and athlete assessment illustrating the new method and showing that a system's quality performance, calculated by the traditional GPA index, may lead to different assessment conclusions.

articleTitle: Keynote Speech I: Microsoft AI
publicationTitle: 2018 28th International Conference on Computer Theory and Applications (ICCTA)
abstract: Summary form only given, as follows. The complete presentation was not made available for publication as part of the conference proceedings. Put simply, AI is a machine's ability to recognize images and words, learn and reason in ways that are similar to what people do. Our AI systems are designed to augment what people do. Our goal is to make AI available to everyone. And we're committed to making sure that our AI tools and technologies earn the trust of all. AI is already having a tangible, useful impact on many people's day-to-day lives, whether it's helping someone quickly create an impressive PowerPoint presentation or providing a plainspoken answer to your Bing search query. As part of our AI for Good initiative, farmers are figuring out how to grow more food using fewer natural resources. Because of AI systems that detect malware and automatically protect computers against it, Windows is more secure. AI isn't new to Microsoft. In fact, computer scientists at Microsoft and elsewhere have been working on AI technologies for decades.

articleTitle: Performance Comparison of Intrusion Detection Machine Learning Classifiers on Benchmark and New Datasets
publicationTitle: 2018 28th International Conference on Computer Theory and Applications (ICCTA)
abstract: With the tremendous growth of the Internet and the continuous increase in malicious attacks on corporate networks, Intrusion Detection Systems (IDS) have been designed and adopted by organizations to accurately detect intrusion and other malicious activities. But these IDSs still suffer from setbacks such as False Positives (FP), low detection accuracy and False Negatives (FN). To enhance the performance of IDSs, machine learning classifiers are used to aid detection accuracy and greatly reduce the false positive and false negative rate. In this research we have evaluated six classifiers such as Decision Tree (J48), Random Forest (RF), K-Nearest Neighbor (K-NN), Nave Bayes (NB), Support Vector Machine (SVM) and Artificial Neural Networks (ANN) on three different types of datasets such as NSL-KDD, UNSW-NB15 and Phishing dataset. Our results show that K-NN and J48 are the best performing classifiers when it comes to detection accuracy, testing time and false positive rate.

articleTitle: Enhance Job Candidate Learning Path using Gamification
publicationTitle: 2018 28th International Conference on Computer Theory and Applications (ICCTA)
abstract: There is a gap between the graduates learning path and job market requirements. Different recruitments WebPages focus on the match between the candidate and the job without focusing on defining the actual level of the candidate in the career and the whether this candidate can enhance his learning path to match more job vacancies or even match different job field. Gamification is used nowadays to motivate the learner to study and even it is used in working daily activities. In this paper a job matching model is proposed (matching the candidate personal and educational details with Information and Communication Technology - National Competency framework (ICT-NCF) with the ability to enhance the candidate learning path that will develop also his career path using Gamification tools.

articleTitle: Predictive analytics for loan default in banking sector using machine learning techniques
publicationTitle: 2018 28th International Conference on Computer Theory and Applications (ICCTA)
abstract: The early prediction of loan default in banks is a critical area nowadays. Machine learning techniques are being used to predict and classify the loan applicant as defaulter or not before granting him the loan. Several types of statistical and artificial intelligent classification techniques can be used to predict the loan default of bank's customers. However, ensemble machine learning techniques are introduced to perform better than traditional statistical and AI techniques as it combines several base models to produce one optimal predictive model with better performance and accuracy. A comparative study is applied on different machine learning techniques on customer's loans dataset obtained from a public bank's database that contains customer's loans and personal data. The data is processed and analyzed using Apache Spark, a machine learning tool for big data processing. The results of the proposed system is evaluated by seven performance metrics to compare the performance of each classifier and find out the best performing one among them. It is found out that the ensemble machine learning techniques has better performance than single base classifiers in predicting the loan default.

articleTitle: A New Approach for Pressure Sore Prevention
publicationTitle: 2018 28th International Conference on Computer Theory and Applications (ICCTA)
abstract: This paper presents a novel method for preventing pressure ulcer for medical use. A unique bed-Chair mechanical structure is introduced, where the system is automatically controlled to reduce pressure and the patient's main contact areas. The mechanical system is described and modeled mathematically. Two control systems are compared to show the performance of the system in each case: classical PID controller and Adaptive model Predictive Control (MPC). An online recursive least square identification algorithm (RLS) was used for extracting the time varied model of Pressure ulcer. The MPC achieved the objectives, constraints and safety rules of the medical requirements of the Pressure ulcer. The results of the simulation illustrates the performance comparison between both controllers.

articleTitle: Neuro Fuzzy DC-DC Converter
publicationTitle: 2018 28th International Conference on Computer Theory and Applications (ICCTA)
abstract: These days, on account of the immense advances in energy technology, sustainable power source has developed and turned into an essential part of the power system. However, the output energy that is collected from the natural surrounding elements is unstable, therefore this paper presents a DC-DC Buck-Boost Converter to control and manage the Energy Harvester output voltage via Neuro-fuzzy controller to provide constant output voltage for various power system applications among them are: self-sustainable Wireless Sensor Node. Based on adaptive Neuro-Fuzzy inference systems (ANFIS), this methodology combines the training talents of artificial neural networks and also the ability of fuzzy logic to handle imprecise knowledge. The execution of the proposed strategy is contrasted with that of a PID-like Fuzzy controller to exhibit its adequacy and it has proven that there is an effective changes regarding settling time almost being zero, overshoot being negligible and steady state voltage. The simulation results are determined by means that of MATLAB/Simulink toolbox.

articleTitle: Secure Translation Using Fully Homomorphic Encryption and Sequence-to-Sequence Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2018 28th International Conference on Computer Theory and Applications (ICCTA)
abstract: Working with confidential data and classified letters is very sensitive. Any operation on such data (e.g. archiving, transferring, and translating) is subject to strict rules; one of these important rules is to avoid any untrusted copy of such data. Political and governmental affairs are mainly dependent on full security of the related information especially when it comes to text translation. This paper is proposing a solution and a proof of concept for secured translation through a combination between Sequence-to-Sequence Neural Network and Homomorphic encryption, where neural network is trained on the plaintext. During the production, we feed the encoder with the encrypted text as well as the public key used for encryption and the decoder will generate the translated text in an encryption format which will be decrypted using the private key hosted at client side. The proposed work is verified using a large dataset of English and Arabic words. The results show that the output of the translation is not affected at all under the secure mode (after encryption of the input words) in comparison to the normal mode (without encryption.) However, the computational complexity is much increased.

articleTitle: Unclonable key Generator Based on Chip signature and SRAM-PUF of ATmega328P chip
publicationTitle: 2018 28th International Conference on Computer Theory and Applications (ICCTA)
abstract: Embedded devices are now taking over the world, their presence in everyone's pocket and home arouses questions around privacy and security concerns. What amplifies these concerns are the rapid spread of internet of things (IOT) devices and smart meters across the world. These devices become a target for attackers to compromise a device, or embed parasites on an authorized network. These kinds of attacks require an innovative method of authentication to protect unwanted parties from presence in an authorized network and its consequences from violating user's privacy and other effects. This paper proposes a novel approach for using the ATmega328p microcontroller to generate an unclonable key based on the chip signature and manufacturing stored data as well as the static random access memory to act as a physically unclonable function (SRAM-PUF) of the Atmega328P chip. The generated key has been subjected to different statistical tests. A proof of concept model has been successfully built to test a suggested authentication scheme between two devices. It takes four steps, at the most, to accomplish the authentication process with a time of 90 ms for a key length of 256 bit

articleTitle: Application of the Grey System Theory to Assessment with Approximate Data
publicationTitle: 2018 28th International Conference on Computer Theory and Applications (ICCTA)
abstract: The Grey System theory introduced by Deng in 1982 has been nowadays proved to be an effective tool for studying systems with “poor” information data (uncertain, incomplete, etc.) In the present research Grey Numbers are used as tools for evaluating a system's mean performance when utilizing qualitative grades and not numerical scores for this purpose. Although this new assessment method is proved to be equivalent with an analogous method using Triangular Fuzzy Numbers as tools developed in an earlier work, it reduces the required computational burden, since it requires the calculation of two components only (instead of three in the case of the Triangular Fuzzy Numbers) for obtaining the mean value of the Grey Numbers involved. Examples are also presented on student and athlete assessment illustrating the new method and showing that a system's quality performance, calculated by the traditional GPA index, may lead to different assessment conclusions.

articleTitle: Enhancing AES Algorithm with DNA Computing
publicationTitle: 2018 28th International Conference on Computer Theory and Applications (ICCTA)
abstract: DNA cryptography is a modern promising path in cryptography research that surfaced with the improvement in Deoxyribonucleic Acid (DNA) computing field. Traditional cryptographic systems have an extended legacy and are designed on a solid mathematical and theoretical basis. Thus, an important notion must be developed that the DNA cryptography is never to negate the tradition, but to make a bridge between existing and new technology. The strength of DNA computing will fortify the existing security systems by checking up a new probability of the hybrid cryptographic system. This paper aims to present a proposed DNA sequence enhanced Advanced Encryption standard (AES) design. The proposed algorithm has been implemented with all its features (data, algorithms operations and used functions) on DNA sequence rather than bits in mix column step. The proposed technique demonstrates the possibility of building such an intricate system of DNA sequence in a method for making it an appropriate contender for usage in the biological environment or on DNA computers. The presented algorithm keeps a security quality and strength of the standard algorithm. The assessment of the presented method is carried out using MATLAB 2016b. The experimental results show a significant improvement in terms of breaking time for different text file sizes.

articleTitle: Keynote Speech II: Autonomous and Connected Electric Vehicles Deployment in Smart Cities
publicationTitle: 2018 28th International Conference on Computer Theory and Applications (ICCTA)
abstract: Summary form only given, as follows. The complete presentation was not made available for publication as part of the conference proceedings. The transformation of our current cities into smarter cities will bring challenges in diverse areas such as the transportation system, the electricity system, and wearable systems, just to name a few. In smart cities, Information and Communication Technologies (ICT) will play a vital role for providing services in the urban environment. These services include real time monitoring and reaction in time through wireless sensor and actuator networks. Smart Grids (SGs), Intelligent Transportation Systems (ITS), Internet of Things (IoT), Electric Vehicles (EVs), and Wireless Sensor Networks (WSNs) will be the building blocks of futuristic smart cities. All these technologies will help in building smart cities. In this presentation we will address technology trends with a focus on autonomous vehicles and in particular on Connected and Autonomous Electric Vehicles (CAEVs) in smart cities. Current capabilities as well as limitations and opportunities of key enabling technologies will be reviewed, along with a discussion on the impact of such advances on society and the environment. Predictions about changes in the car-industry will be discussed, including potential industry winners and losers.

articleTitle: A Modified Multinomial Platform Architecture for Computer Adaptive Testing (CAT)
publicationTitle: 2018 28th International Conference on Computer Theory and Applications (ICCTA)
abstract: This research introduces a web-based platform that enables generating fully customizable CAT examinations. Such platform is based on most flexible, newly introduced web technologies; NodeJS. It is a fast and efficient web server for web applications. The architecture is structured using Modified Multinomial Model (MMM). MMM has been identified as one of the best models that succeeded to grant results resembling real examinees' abilities and the best model with least item exposure issue. The structure and outline of the architecture are introduced to demonstrate the traits and attributes of the existing approach.

articleTitle: Evaluation of virtual machine scheduling algorithms within Cloud environment
publicationTitle: 2018 28th International Conference on Computer Theory and Applications (ICCTA)
abstract: Migration schedulers of data centers have an important impact on cost, energy consumption and service qualities. Several virtual machines are migrated inside a datacenter to stabilize the load, save energy or make construction servers for maintenance. This paper presents a comparison of Virtual Machine (VM) scheduling within cloud environment. The objective of this paper is to demonstrate that the choice of VM Scheduling algorithm in Cloud computing model implicitly improves the application performance under resource and service demand variations. We will discuss different VM schedulers implemented and their performance analysis in Virtual environment of cloud computing in order to achieve better the energy consumption using GreenCloud simulator.

articleTitle: Application of pattern recognition algorithms in assessing phytoequivalency of phytomedicines using NMR metabolomics data: A case study of artichoke
publicationTitle: 2018 28th International Conference on Computer Theory and Applications (ICCTA)
abstract: In compliance with strict regulations of botanicals standardisation which are sought to assure the integrity and efficacy of phytopharmaceuticals, metabolite profiling aided by pattern recognition (PR) analysis are highly valued tools to meet such need. Spectroscopic and chromatographic methods used for the metabolomic analysis of botanical material and its derived commercial pharmaceuticals generate huge datasets that need to be modeled using adequate PR methods. In most cases, PR analyses such as principal component analysis (PCA) and partial least squares-discriminant analysis (PLS-DA) are routinely employed to extract maximum information from these analytical datasets. More accurate and reliable prediction of phytoequivalency and different quality issues are now achievable by these computationally-modelled metabolomics data. We present herein a novel approach for assessing phytoequivalency of botanicals using artichoke leaves as a case study where different pattern recognition tools were explored for modelling proton nuclear magnetic spectral data of artichoke preparations. Using this approach, the variable efficacy encountered with some phytomedicines can be tackled in a more robust and automated manner.

articleTitle: Modeling Municipal Solid Waste Management System with Consideration of the Informal Sector
publicationTitle: 2018 28th International Conference on Computer Theory and Applications (ICCTA)
abstract: Municipal Solid Waste management (MSWM) in developing countries faces a number of challenges and obstacles. One of the main characteristics differentiating it from other developed countries is the presence of the informal sector. This paper develops a mathematical model to study the effect of informal sector on the MSWM system economic performance. The proposed model is validated via a numerical illustration. The results give insights to decision makers about the economic effect of integrating the informal waste sector in the MSWM system

articleTitle: Numerical Solution of One Dimensional Generalized Thermoelastic Problem by Using Adomian's Decomposition Method and Laplace's Transform Method
publicationTitle: 2018 28th International Conference on Computer Theory and Applications (ICCTA)
abstract: This work deals with the numerical solution of one-dimension generalized thermoelasticity with one relaxation time problem under given initial and boundary conditions. The methods are based on two different techniques; Laplace's transforms method and the Adomian's decomposition method. The numerical results have been calculated for the two methods with two different cases of the relaxation time parameter. The comparisons between the results of the two methods have been represented in tables and figures. The outputs of the two methods are much closed. The Adomian's decomposition method is successful numerical method for generalized thermoelasticity models.

articleTitle: Gamified Mathematics Learning for K 12
publicationTitle: 2018 28th International Conference on Computer Theory and Applications (ICCTA)
abstract: Most of students think that mathematics is a difficult, complicated and confusing subject because it involves formulae and calculations. Most children see mathematic as a boring subject and there is no relationship between learning mathematics and its application to society. This paper explores the use of gamification in mathematics learning for children in order to increase their engagement and motivation in learning mathematics. Experiments have been conducted on various students' categories to demonstrate the efficiency of the proposed gamified mathematics learning method. The experimental results show an outstanding performance in the terms of students' progress improvement compared with others who used traditional learning methodology. Various experiments have been carried out to demonstrate the robustness of the proposed gamified method.

articleTitle: Multi-step Ahead Time Series Prediction via Bagging Trees Based Neighborhood
publicationTitle: 2018 28th International Conference on Computer Theory and Applications (ICCTA)
abstract: Locality based prediction has shown excellent performance in difficult multi-step forecasting problems. However, either neighbor search or sparse coding is usually used to define locality, which requires considerable computations. In this paper, we are investigating a locality-based time series forecasting based on bagging trees defined neighborhood. The proposed method is based on finding all the training examples that share the same leaves in the bagging trees ensemble with the test vector. Then we calculate the predicted target value based on the training examples respective weights (how many times each training example share the same terminal node in each tree with the test example). Two types of bagging trees are investigated; (classification and regression). We test our proposed method on the monthly time series data from M3 competition dataset with horizons range (1 to 18). We compare our results with other machine learning and statistical forecasting techniques. The proposed model outperformed almost all other techniques especially in higher horizons.

articleTitle: A Computer Simulator to Study the effect of the Spiral curves on driver's speed behavior on Two-Lane Rural Highway
publicationTitle: 2018 28th International Conference on Computer Theory and Applications (ICCTA)
abstract: There are many studies that have been conducted to improve the highway design consistency. Most of these studies are based on spot speed data collection, which is done by measuring the speed at specific locations such as in the middle of the tangent and the center of the horizontal curve. However, the maximum and minimum speeds don't correspond to the center of tangents and curves, respectively. In this study, a computer simulator was used to produce a continues speed profile to facilitate analyzing the driver speed behavior for various pathway scenarios. In the current stage of development, the focus was to evaluate the effect of the transition (spiral) curve existence in the highway alignment on the driver speed magnitude. Measurement is taken at five specific locations for each segment of the tested two-lane highway. These points are located before, during and after the curve. A comparison was made to illustrate the role of spiral curve existence on the magnitude of driver's speed. Using this comparison, the usefulness of the alignment with transition curve can be evaluated in contrast to the alignment without transition curve. The following variables were considered in this analysis: 1) curve radius, 2) deflection angle and 3) direction of driving. Briefly., the usefulness of the spiral curve was significant in the small curves and big deflection angles.

articleTitle: DNA Computing Modeling of HEMT transistor Noise Parameters
publicationTitle: 2018 28th International Conference on Computer Theory and Applications (ICCTA)
abstract: As is well known noise figure plays an important role for many applications, so this paper will introduce a noise model for heterojunction transistors new technique for prediction. A presented neural network model with cascade feed-forward training algorithm has been connected to foresee heterojunction microwave transistor noise parameters then applying the new technique to get the higher accuracy for noise parameters using DNA computing. This model depends on the operating frequency, temperature and bias conditions. A neural system design is displayed to encourage the expectation exactness of the presented show. The Model accuracy has been demonstrated by coordinating anticipated and estimated values of heterojunction transistors for a specific data set of noise parameters at various frequencies, temperatures and bias points. Here the design will be to investigative noise model of an AlGaAs/InGaAs/GaAs Hetrojunction transistor. It is shown that introducing DNA computing enhances the obtained values for noise figure, and also gives higher accuracy for prediction of the four parameters required by using one neural network for this purpose. It is also shown that only one neural network for simulation of noise figure parameters was used, without using a special network for Rn/50 values, so it's clear that DNA not only enhances the values but ails saved time and neural networks.

articleTitle: Keynote Speech IV: Knowledge Engineering Paradigms in Smart Education: Methodologies, Applications and Challenges
publicationTitle: 2018 28th International Conference on Computer Theory and Applications (ICCTA)
abstract: Summary form only given, as follows. The complete presentation was not made available for publication as part of the conference proceedings. Knowledge engineering paradigms (KEPs) deal with the development of intelligent systems in which reasoning and knowledge play pivotal role. Knowledge engineering (KE) includes; Knowledge acquisition, knowledge representation and management, Knowledge discovery, intelligent shells and tools, smart methodologies, Knowledge modelling, Knowledge compilation, knowledge-based systems and ontological engineering. KEPs provide a robust intelligent computing techniques and algorithms that can help solving problems in a variety of domains and tasks. Recently, KEPs receive increasing attention within the fields of education and learning. Researchers have been used the knowledge engineering (KE) techniques and methodologies to develop a smart tutoring and learning systems. Moreover, the convergence of artificial intell igence (AI) and web science is enabling the creation of a new generation of web-based smart systems for all educational and learning tasks. This talk discusses the KE and AI paradigms for developing the intelligent educational and smart Learning systems. Four most popular paradigms are discussed namely; case-based reasoning, ontological engineering, data mining and intelligent agents. Moreover, the talk addresses the challenges faced by the application develop ers and knowledge engineers in developing and deploying such systems. In addition, the talk presents some cases of intelligent learning systems/tools developed by the author and his colleagues at Artificial intelligence and Knowledge Engineering Research Labs, Ain Shams University, AIKE Labs-ASU, Cairo, Egypt.

articleTitle: Improving Performance of Robust and Efficient E-Learning Platform Using Distributed Computing Technologies for Saudi Arabia's Institutes
publicationTitle: 2018 28th International Conference on Computer Theory and Applications (ICCTA)
abstract: There are robust techniques and tools used in E-Learning in Saudi Arabia's institutes, but these techniques and tools are not sufficient in all the fields of E-learning. So that more computing power, storage capacity are needed. The use of large data in E- learning puts importance pressure on power computing and data storage. The Cloud computing paradigm, as an Information Technology (IT) platform is proposed to solve our problem. Experimental results clearly validated that Cloud computing technology and Amazon Elastic Compute Cloud (EC2) constitute an adequate infrastructures for building a powerful E-Learning tools and enhancing large E-Learning performances.

articleTitle: Towards a Multidimensional Model for Terrorist Attacks Analysis and Mining
publicationTitle: 2018 28th International Conference on Computer Theory and Applications (ICCTA)
abstract: Terrorist attacks are in exponentially growth and cause daily dire human and material damages. Analyzing potential terrorism data is without doubt an indispensable task not only to understand these terrorist events, mainly terrorist implicated actors, their communities and their operation methods and tactics, but also to predict future attacks. However, terrorist events are commonly conducted differently and rarely fit the models of conventional attacks. Thus, terrorist events are usually hard to analyze, mine and investigate. In this paper, we propose a multidimensional model, named Terrorist Data Warehouse (TerDW), for allowing terrorist investigators to perform interesting and specific analysis for decision-making objectives. Practically, while consulting gathered information relative to specific terrorist attacks, such as attacks' locations, dates, used weapons, and implicated attackers, investigators can query the proposed data warehouse (TerDW) using multidimensional queries. The proposed model is based on consistent dimensions and measures. Terrorist attacks data are extracted from Global Terrorism Database (GTD), a well-known database that includes information about terrorist events that took place from 1970 to 2017. Examples of queries have been conducted to evaluate the efficiency of the proposed model. The queries' results demonstrate clearly that the proposed model allows investigators to carry out more appropriate multidimensional analysis, investigations and decisions.

articleTitle: CloudWar: A new schema for securing and querying data warehouse hosted in the cloud
publicationTitle: 2018 28th International Conference on Computer Theory and Applications (ICCTA)
abstract: With the growth of cloud computing, data warehouse can benefit from this new technology. Cloud storage holds the advantages of high reliability, simple management and cost-effective. However, as each technological advance, the cloud computing also brings its own risks, data security issues are one of the top concerns when dealing with sensitive data. To ensure the confidentiality of sensitive data, the owner must encrypt it before outsourcing. When data are encrypted, a tradeo □ must be achieved between security and performance. Existing solutions are not suitable for cloud data warehouse because those solutions induce a heavy overhead in terms of data storage and query performance. So because the nature of data warehouse, a suitable solution must be proposed that balances the security and the performance of data warehouse hosted in the cloud. In this paper, we propose (CloudWar) an efficient schema based on a homomorphic encryption algorithm for securing and querying a data warehouse hosted in the cloud. CloudWar addresses the short coming of existing approaches by reducing the volume overhead and time complexity of query processing will still maintaining good privacy and performance. Also, this new schema proposes a new signature for verifying the integrity of data when received from the cloud. Theoretical and experimental results show the efficiency of CloudWar in terms of privacy and performance with respect to other solutions.

articleTitle: The Impact of Using Inbound Open Innovation Product Platforming by Egyptian SMEs on New Software Product Introduction
publicationTitle: 2018 28th International Conference on Computer Theory and Applications (ICCTA)
abstract: The focus of this paper is in the area of Open Innovation with its uses in Software Industry. Such a study is important to investigate the impact of using Inbound Open Innovation product platforming on new software product introduction by SMEs located in Egypt where minimal researches were conducted. The population was Egyptian SMEs that works in the software industry. The findings from this study are from Binary Logistic Regression results and provide evidence that there is an insignificant relation between the use of Inbound Open Innovation Product Platforming and New Software Product Introduction by Egyptian SMEs. The main conclusion drawn from this study is companies if not educated enough and fully aware about the technicality and functionality of the Open Innovation “externally developed” platform used and have a good understanding of how they will build their product upon it, they can't obtain the full benefits from using it. This study recommends for any future study to separate each platform technology, with two group of companies the one who use it and the others who are not, this would provide a more accurate measurement of company awareness of the platform technology used and would also lead to having significant results in return. The study also recommends for SMEs' decision makers to have good awareness about the software product requirements specification and Open Innovation platform features, for efficiently building their new product.

Index Terms: Results Of The Binary Logistic Regression
Author Keywords: the Introduction of New Software Product

articleTitle: Modified Elliptic Curve Cryptography in Wireless Sensor Networks Security
publicationTitle: 2018 28th International Conference on Computer Theory and Applications (ICCTA)
abstract: Our world converts to a huge urn of digital data through wireless networks. Since the beginning of the third Millennium, wireless sensor networks created an increasing attention to military applications, industrial applications, and research viewpoints. It is necessary to deliver security to the information that to share over the wireless networks. In addition, wireless sensor network nodes are resources constrained, such as restricted battery energy, limited computational operations, and small memory size. Elliptic curve cryptography is the best appropriate algorithm for wireless sensor network as it provides better security for minimal key sizes, faster computations, reductions in processing power, minimal storage space, and low bandwidth rate consumption. However, Elliptic Curve's main problem is that the encoding expends more resources, needs for additional memory, and more encryption time. This paper introduces a novel algorithm is suitable to secure exchanging data of wireless sensor network.

articleTitle: Caching Techniques for Flight Delays Prediction in Big Data Using SparkR
publicationTitle: 2018 28th International Conference on Computer Theory and Applications (ICCTA)
abstract: Over the past years, Flight delays had negative effects on passengers, airlines, and airports. Now it is possible to predict that a flight will be delayed based on the statistics of past flights. In this work, a new Dynamic Prediction of the Departure and Arrival Flight Delays (DPDAD) model is created to get the prediction and the probability of delay status in origin and destination airports using certain airline through a website even before booking an airline ticket and suggesting the top ten carriers for the same flight. Most of the previous studies focused on flights departure delay only or arrival delay only. This work focused on both delays at the same time which helps a user to take a better decision. Spark is used as an ecosystem cluster over a Hadoop cluster; it is handled through a SparkR library from R. Most of related works examined the importance of caching in Apache Spark but this work examined Caching storage Techniques and detected that best caching storage depends on ML technique and how it accesses the data when it is overloaded.
